INFRA_docs.goal: tools/README.md covers booting both profiles, every script, the app-password-over-http caveat, the posture-injection mechanism, live plugin mounting, and wiring .x-agent.json.

decisions.what: Use @wp-playground/cli 3.1.50 via its exported runCLI() rather than shelling out to the wp-playground-cli binary.
decisions.why: Docker is installed but not running on this machine, so wp-env is not viable. runCLI({command:'server'}) returns a RunCLIServer with { playground, server, serverUrl } and an asyncDispose, which is what makes it possible to (a) run PHP inside the *same* instance that is serving HTTP and (b) tear down deterministically. Verified: package.json exports '.' -> index.js which re-exports runCLI from run-cli.d.ts; the type signature runCLI(args & {command:'server'}): Promise<RunCLIServer> is in node_modules/@wp-playground/cli/run-cli.d.ts.

decisions.what: Provision users and application passwords with playground.run({code}) after the server is up, not with a separate `wp-playground-cli php` process.
decisions.why: A separate CLI process is a different WordPress instance with a different database. Verified that playground.run() shares state with the HTTP request handler: created a user via run(), then authenticated as that user over HTTP with curl in the same boot and got 200. This works because the CLI's worker threads share a native site directory (bootRequestHandler takes nativeInternalDirPath and a FileLockManager).

decisions.what: Enable Application Passwords over plain http via a boot-generated mu-plugin filtering wp_is_application_passwords_available and wp_is_application_passwords_available_for_user to true.
decisions.why: WordPress gates Application Passwords on is_ssl(); the sandbox is http://127.0.0.1:<port>, so without the filter the whole Basic-auth half of CONTRACT.md is untestable. Generating the file from boot.mjs (rather than asking a human to place it) keeps the override scoped to the sandbox: it lives in tools/.runtime/work/<key>/mu-plugins/, is rewritten every boot, and never enters either plugin's source tree. Verified: with the filter, curl -u user:app_password against /wp/v2/users/me returns 200 and anonymous returns 401. Documented as sandbox-only in tools/README.md.

decisions.what: Inject X_COMPANION_POSTURE primarily through Playground's php.defineConstant() (RunCLIArgs.define), with a guarded mu-plugin as a second path.
decisions.why: Verified by experiment which mechanisms are visible to an HTTP request: --define/define (php.defineConstant) IS visible, and it applies before wp-config.php, i.e. earlier than mu-plugins and earlier than plugins; blueprint-level `constants` and a defineWpConfigConsts step with method rewrite-wp-config are also visible. Chose define because it needs no on-disk rewrite and survives a wiped site directory. The mu-plugin (000-x-posture.php, wrapped in if(!defined())) is the fallback for processes that do not go through the CLI's --define, which the CLI help explicitly calls process-specific. boot.mjs asserts the constant inside the sandbox after boot and refuses to return an instance whose posture does not match the request.

decisions.what: Mount plugin directories with the CLI's after-install `mount` (host dir -> /wordpress/wp-content/plugins/<dirname>) and activate them with an appended blueprint activatePlugin step.
decisions.why: Verified with --help on `server`: --mount takes /host/path:/vfs/path and is applied after WordPress installs but before blueprint steps run, so activatePlugin can see the mounted plugin. Verified the mount is a live filesystem view, not a copy: edited a mounted PHP file on the host mid-run and the next HTTP request returned the new behaviour with no restart. This is the property the plugin authors care about most.

decisions.what: Always mount a host directory at /wordpress via mount-before-install, so siteDir in the runtime JSON is a real path.
decisions.why: The `server` command otherwise keeps the site in a temp dir that is not exposed to the caller. Verified: with mount-before-install the WordPress install lands in the host dir (wp-load.php, wp-content/database present) and a second boot with wordpressInstallMode=install-from-existing-files-if-needed reuses it, cutting boot from ~7s to ~2.3s. --persist keeps the dir; without it the dir is wiped so the proof suite never inherits state.

decisions.what: Blueprint v1 declarations, validated against the schema validator shipped in @wp-playground/blueprints.
decisions.why: Step names and shapes were read out of node_modules/@wp-playground/blueprints/blueprint-schema.json (definitions.StepDefinition.oneOf) rather than guessed: activateTheme{themeFolderName}, setSiteOptions{options}, installPlugin{pluginData,options}, activatePlugin{pluginPath}, runPHP{code}, defineWpConfigConsts{consts,method}. Both profile blueprints were run through the package's own blueprint-schema-validator.js and report valid=true.

decisions.what: core-plus-suite installs Kadence Blocks with options.onError='throw' AND boot.mjs re-asserts the plugin is active afterwards.
decisions.why: The profile must fail loudly rather than silently degrade to core-only. Verified working online: 175 registered block types of which 59 are kadence/*. The double check means a future change in how a failed download is reported still cannot produce a mislabelled instance.

decisions.what: boot.mjs detaches by default: the parent spawns itself with --__daemon, waits on a ready file keyed by a boot id, prints the runtime JSON and exits.
decisions.why: The natural shell idiom is `RT=$(node tools/playground/boot.mjs ... --json)` followed by curl, which requires the booting process to exit while the server keeps serving. --foreground keeps the old behaviour for interactive use, and proof/lib/env.mjs boots in-process so withInstance can dispose deterministically.

decisions.what: Extend the CONTRACT.md §5 fallback trigger from '404' to '404 that is not a rest_* JSON error, or any 3xx'.
decisions.why: Measured against an instance booted with --permalinks plain: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users/me returns 301 (WordPress canonical-redirects it), not 404, while /?rest_route=/wp/v2/users/me returns 200. A strict 404-only rule would never fall back on a plain-permalink site. The rest_* JSON check keeps a genuinely missing route (rest_no_route, which arrives as a 404 with a JSON body) from being misread as a permalink problem.

decisions.what: In proof/lib/env.mjs, authenticate the Playwright context with BOTH browser.newContext({httpCredentials}) and extraHTTPHeaders: { Authorization: Basic ... }.
decisions.why: httpCredentials alone does not authenticate a page navigation against WordPress, including with send:'always'. Chromium only replays Basic credentials after a 401 carrying WWW-Authenticate, and the WP REST API returns rest_forbidden 401s without that header. Measured: page.goto -> 401 with httpCredentials only (both with and without send/origin); 200 with the explicit header; context.request.get -> 200 either way, which is what makes the difference easy to miss. extraHTTPHeaders also covers sub-resource requests the harness page makes back to the REST API, which CONTRACT.md §6 requires.

Chromium build 1223 is already in ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright on this machine, and 1.60.0 is the release that expects 1223 (checked playwright-core@<v>/browsers.json for 1.55-1.61: 1187/1194/1200/1208/1217/1223/1228). 1.62.1 wanted chromium-1234 and would have forced a browser download.

decisions.what: Probe port availability by binding the wildcard address, not 127.0.0.1.
decisions.why: Playground's Express server binds :: (dual stack). A probe bound to 127.0.0.1 reported an occupied port as free and the boot then died with EADDRINUSE on :::9400.

decisions.what: Flush stdout before process.exit() in wpcall.mjs and boot.mjs.
decisions.why: process.exit() truncates asynchronous pipe writes. A 947 KB /wp/v2/block-types response was being cut mid-JSON when piped to jq; writing through a callback and only then exiting fixes it.

decisions.what: Deterministic default ports 9400/9401/9402/9403 for core-only|core-plus-suite x toolchain|production, scanning to 9450 when taken.
decisions.why: The proof suite needs a production-posture instance running next to a toolchain one to assert posture_forbidden, and predictable ports make ad-hoc curl during development possible without reading the runtime file first.

deviations.what: boot.mjs takes --mu-plugin (not --muPlugin) on the command line; the programmatic option is muPlugins: string[]. Both spellings are accepted on the CLI.
deviations.why: Consistency with --plugin and normal CLI casing.

deviations.what: The runtime JSON carries exactly the keys the brief specified. Extra bookkeeping (port, pid file, log, mounts, active plugins) lives in tools/.runtime/<key>.pid, <key>.log and the in-process return value of boot(), not in the descriptor.
deviations.why: The brief said 'prints, with --json, exactly' that object, and other tools parse it.

deviations.what: Added --permalinks pretty|plain to boot.mjs, which is not in the brief.
deviations.why: Playground boots with pretty permalinks, so nothing would ever exercise the ?rest_route= half of CONTRACT.md §5. It is how the fallback was proven, and it lets the proof suite assert both branches.

deviations.what: wp-env is not implemented. Only the Playground backend exists.
deviations.why: Docker is installed but not running on this machine (established before the work started); an untested wp-env path would be worse than an absent one. tools/README.md records what a wp-env backend would have to reproduce.

deviations.what: tools/ has its own package.json and node_modules rather than using a repo-root manifest.
deviations.why: The repo root is not in this agent's file ownership. proof/lib/env.mjs resolves playwright through createRequire anchored at tools/package.json so it works regardless of the caller's cwd.
